import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Smallest power with base>1 and exponent $n$ without digit 0

For statistical reasons it is conjectured that the sequence is finite.
Also it is conjectured that $a(40)$ does not exist (i.e. the sequence is empty for $n=40$).

*References:*
- [A103662](https://oeis.org/A103662)
-/

namespace OeisA103662

open Nat List Set

/--
A helper predicate: $b^n$ is a power with base $>1$ whose decimal representation
does not contain the digit 0.
We assume $n$ is the exponent, $n \ge 1$.
-/
def IsValidZerolessPower (n b : ℕ) : Prop :=
  b > 1 ∧ 0 ∉ digits 10 (b ^ n)

/--
The primary defining sequence `a`.
`a n` is the smallest power with base $>1$ and exponent $n$ whose decimal representation
doesn't contain the digit 0.
$$a(n) = (\min \{ b \in \mathbb{N} \mid b > 1,
  \text{decimal representation of } b^n \text{ contains no digit } 0 \})^n$$
If no such base exists, `sInf` of an empty set of naturals returns 0, so `a n = 0`.
-/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let smallestBase := sInf { b | IsValidZerolessPower n b }
  smallestBase ^ n

/-- Term theorems verifying the first few values of the sequence against the official OEIS b-file -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by
  constructor

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 2 := by
  simp_all[a]
  norm_num[Iff,IsValidZerolessPower]
  exact ( IsLeast.csInf_eq ⟨.symm (by norm_num), fun and => And.left⟩)

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 4 := by
  norm_num[a]
  delta IsValidZerolessPower
  exact (congr_arg) (.^2) (IsLeast.csInf_eq ⟨.symm (by norm_num), fun and=>And.left⟩)

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 8 := by
  norm_num[a]
  delta IsValidZerolessPower
  exact (.trans (by
    rw [IsLeast.csInf_eq (by use ⟨by constructor, by norm_num⟩, fun and' => And.left)])
    (by constructor))

/--
For statistical reasons it is conjectured that the sequence is finite.
This is formalized as the assertion that for large enough $n$, no valid zeroless power exists,
which in our definition results in $a(n) = 0$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n > N → a n = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
$a(40)$, if it exists, is not known.

This claim is rooted in the finiteness conjecture. The most direct mathematical expression
of the open problem concerning $a(40)$ is the negation of the existence of a valid base.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture.variants.a_40 :
  ¬ ∃ (b : ℕ), IsValidZerolessPower 40 b := by
  sorry

end OeisA103662

findings.description: The statement `∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n > N → a n = 0` requires every sufficiently large exponent to lack a valid base. This is equivalent to finiteness of the entire set `{n | ∃ b, IsValidZerolessPower n b}`. However, OEIS explicitly defines its finiteness conjecture here as the existence of some exponent with no valid base. Requiring eventual absence strengthens that existential claim; it is not merely a different encoding of a missing term. The zero convention itself is sound: Lean confirms `a n = 0 ↔ ¬ ∃ b, IsValidZerolessPower n b` for every `n`.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A103662, M. F. Hasler's comment dated March 8, 2014: “Finite means here that for some n, no such power > 1 exists. This might be the case already for n=40.” Entry: https://oeis.org/A103662; text read through the official mirror at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A103/A103662.seq.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the statement with `theorem conjecture : ∃ n : ℕ, a n = 0 := by sorry`, or equivalently `∃ n : ℕ, ¬ ∃ b : ℕ, IsValidZerolessPower n b`. Update the docstring to say “for some exponent” rather than “for large enough n”. Such a witness is automatically positive because `a 0 = 1`. If eventual absence is also intended, state it separately with a reference supporting that stronger conjecture.

reformulations.difference: Lean raises the minimum admissible base to the exponent instead of directly minimizing the admissible powers, and represents a nonexistent term by 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed natural exponent n, the map b ↦ b^n is monotone, so the minimum admissible base yields the minimum admissible power. A nonempty admissible-base set has a minimum greater than 1, whose power is positive. If that set is empty, n cannot be 0, since every base greater than 1 is valid at exponent 0; consequently the empty-set infimum gives 0^n = 0. Thus the totalized definition preserves all existing terms and detects nonexistence exactly. In scratch.lean I proved both equality with the infimum of the admissible powers and `a n = 0 ↔ ¬ ∃ b, IsValidZerolessPower n b`, including n = 0.

sources_consulted: OEIS A103662, revision #24 (January 28, 2023), official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A103/A103662.seq
Michel Marcus, A103662 table for n = 0..39: https://oeis.org/A103662/b103662.txt

Repository guidance: /opt/formal-conjectures/STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and AGENTS.md; local answer/category machinery in FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean and FormalConjecturesUtil/Linters/CategoryLinter.lean.
Provided calibration material: past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr01922.md, pr03679.md, pr04987.md, pr00036.md; not_misformalizations/INDEX.md and both supplied cases.
review.notes: Checked all eight declarations. Lean computations matched all 40 published b-file terms; the four existing term proofs have no sorry dependencies. Additional sorry-free checks establish the minimum/zero equivalences and characterize the current main theorem as finiteness of all admissible exponents. The exponent-40 variant is supported by linked entry A103663: its value at 40 is 0, and the entry explicitly says zero values are conjectural. The consulted records still describe the problems as conjectural, so no status issue was found. OEIS's main page and linked Zeroless powers wiki were blocked; the complete sequence entries were obtained from the official OEIS data mirror. Experiments are under /workspace/review/, and the reviewed file is unchanged.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported defect strengthens the source's existential claim to eventual absence, but does not make the formalized statement trivially provable or refutable. The checked equivalences only identify its meaning; finite computations and an abstract counterexample sequence do not decide this assertion about zeroless powers.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created or retained, and no compilation is claimed.
submission.gave_up_reason: I cannot give a short, honest proof or disproof of the only reported declaration. Establishing the quantifier mismatch does not settle the stronger number-theoretic conjecture as formalized.

submission.summary: Replaced eventual vanishing with `∃ n : ℕ, a n = 0`, matching OEIS’s explicit assertion that some exponent has no valid zeroless power. Updated the attached docstring and left all other declarations and attributes unchanged. The requested compile command reports no errors and only the expected `sorry` warnings.
